import pytest

from typesystem.fields import Field
from typesystem.schemas import Schema


class AcceptAnything(Field):
    """A field that accepts any value unchanged."""

    def validate(self, value, *, strict=False):
        return value


class RejectEverything(Field):
    """A field that rejects every value with a known error message."""

    errors = {"bad": "Bad value."}

    def validate(self, value, *, strict=False):
        raise self.validation_error("bad")


class Source:
    """A plain (non-dict) object carrying arbitrary attributes."""

    def __init__(self, **attributes):
        for name, value in attributes.items():
            setattr(self, name, value)


def test_init_from_dict_copies_present_fields_and_ignores_the_rest():
    class Article(Schema):
        title = AcceptAnything()
        body = AcceptAnything()

    article = Article({"title": "Hello", "irrelevant": 42})

    # Fields present in the mapping are set on the instance.
    assert article.title == "Hello"
    # Fields missing from the mapping are left unset.
    assert not hasattr(article, "body")
    # Mapping entries that are not schema fields are ignored.
    assert not hasattr(article, "irrelevant")


def test_init_from_object_copies_matching_attributes_only():
    class Article(Schema):
        title = AcceptAnything()
        body = AcceptAnything()

    article = Article(Source(title="Copied", unrelated="noise"))

    # Attributes matching a field name are copied over.
    assert article.title == "Copied"
    # Attributes with no counterpart on the source are skipped.
    assert not hasattr(article, "body")
    # Source attributes that are not schema fields are ignored.
    assert not hasattr(article, "unrelated")


def test_init_from_kwargs_validates_and_stores_each_value():
    class Profile(Schema):
        username = AcceptAnything()
        email = AcceptAnything()

    profile = Profile(username="alice", email="alice@example.com")

    assert profile.username == "alice"
    assert profile.email == "alice@example.com"


def test_init_falls_back_to_field_defaults():
    class Settings(Schema):
        host = AcceptAnything()
        port = AcceptAnything(default=8080)
        debug = AcceptAnything(default=False)

    settings = Settings(host="localhost")

    # Explicitly passed values win over defaults.
    assert settings.host == "localhost"
    # Missing values fall back to the field defaults.
    assert settings.port == 8080
    assert settings.debug is False

    # A schema whose remaining fields all have defaults can be built bare;
    # fields without defaults (here: host) simply stay unset.
    bare = Settings()
    assert not hasattr(bare, "host")
    assert bare.port == 8080
    assert bare.debug is False


def test_init_with_invalid_value_raises_type_error():
    class Ticket(Schema):
        seat = RejectEverything()

    with pytest.raises(TypeError) as excinfo:
        Ticket(seat="standing")

    message = str(excinfo.value)
    assert message.startswith("Invalid argument 'seat' for Ticket(). ")
    assert "Bad value." in message


def test_init_with_unexpected_kwarg_raises_type_error():
    class Ticket(Schema):
        seat = AcceptAnything()

    with pytest.raises(TypeError) as excinfo:
        Ticket(seat="12A", row="Z")

    assert "'row' is an invalid keyword argument for Ticket()." in str(excinfo.value)


def test_init_rejects_multiple_positional_arguments():
    class Ticket(Schema):
        seat = AcceptAnything()

    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
        Ticket({}, {})


def test_init_rejects_positional_argument_together_with_kwargs():
    class Ticket(Schema):
        seat = AcceptAnything()

    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
        Ticket({}, seat="12A")
